investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigation.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is returning HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", preventing agent creation and causing all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to fail with identical messages. Because the agent is never created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is collected and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation requests for the eval org because the per-org remote agent quota (limit: 100) has been reached. The 409 response is returned before any agent is provisioned, so the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) never succeeds and all downstream evidence collection is skipped. This is a shared upstream dependency failure: all three remote-agents checks call POST /api/agents and all receive the same 409 quota-exceeded response, confirming the failure is at the agent creation layer rather than in any individual check's logic.

This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable when the probe called /api/generate/image/stream. Because the stream terminated at generation_error before any generation_completed frame or image URL could be produced, both required contract assertions failed.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness backing the /api/generate/image/stream SSE endpoint returned a 404 at session-open time in the production-api environment. The stream emitted generation_start followed immediately by generation_error with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version." This caused the stream to terminate without ever emitting a generation_completed frame or an image artifact URL, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract (frameTypes must contain "generation_completed"; imageUrlPresent must equal true). This is an eval-layer failure scoped to the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be asserted.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigations.summary: Every POST /api/agents call made by the remote-agents eval suite is returning HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", preventing agent creation and causing all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to fail with identical messages. Because the agent is never created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is collected and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation requests for the eval org because the per-org remote agent quota (limit: 100) has been reached. The 409 response is returned before any agent is provisioned, so the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) never succeeds and all downstream evidence collection is skipped. This is a shared upstream dependency failure: all three remote-agents checks call POST /api/agents and all receive the same 409 quota-exceeded response, confirming the failure is at the agent creation layer rather than in any individual check's logic.

possibleCauses: Primary: The eval org's remote agent count has reached the swarm-enforced hard limit of 100. Prior eval runs may have created agents that were not cleaned up (e.g., due to withCleanup failures or interrupted runs), causing quota to accumulate over time.
Secondary: A previous eval run left one or more remote agents in a non-terminal state that counts against the quota, and the cleanup path in withCleanup did not delete them before the current run.
Tertiary: The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered on the swarm side, causing previously-acceptable agent counts to now exceed the limit.
Lower probability: The eval service account or org was migrated to a different quota tier with a lower limit, retroactively exceeding the cap.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable when the probe called /api/generate/image/stream. Because the stream terminated at generation_error before any generation_completed frame or image URL could be produced, both required contract assertions failed.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness backing the /api/generate/image/stream SSE endpoint returned a 404 at session-open time in the production-api environment. The stream emitted generation_start followed immediately by generation_error with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version." This caused the stream to terminate without ever emitting a generation_completed frame or an image artifact URL, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract (frameTypes must contain "generation_completed"; imageUrlPresent must equal true). This is an eval-layer failure scoped to the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be asserted.
proof: failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent = false.

failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'
failed-check.message: contract assertion failures — frameTypes expected to contain 'generation_completed'; imageUrlPresent expected true but got false.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2078, well under the warningLatencyMs threshold of 180000, confirming the stream failed fast rather than timing out — consistent with an immediate 404 at session open.
expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains 'generation_completed' and imageUrlPresent equals true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 271–272).

possibleCauses: Primary: The agent runtime harness sidecar or process that serves the /api/generate/image/stream session-open route is not deployed, not running, or is running an incompatible version in the production-api environment, causing the 404 at SESSION_OPEN_FAILED.

Secondary: The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable used by the eval runner is misconfigured or points to a stale/wrong host for the production-api environment, so the correct harness is never reached.

Tertiary: The /api/generate/image/stream route or the session-open sub-route was removed, renamed, or gated behind a feature flag in the production-api deployment, making the endpoint genuinely absent at the path the runner targets.
